The Champion P-class heavy cruiser is a versatile warship featuring a range of powerful energy weapons; the crowning element is a heavy energy turret mounting, rare among Midline ships. This offensive array is backed by a robust energy grid capable of supercharging the energy weapon loadout, increasing damage output to devastating levels. A heavy missile hardpoint complements the loadout, enabling the Champion (P) to unleash a crippling strike without taxing its flux levels. The Champion (P) is a solid and capable contender, able to face capital ships on the battle-line.

A relatively recent design, the Champion is a product of the historically recent Cruiser School. With the discovery of Champion plans aboard a Domain armaments courier, the warship was quickly put into service by the fleets of the Persean League, among others. As it turned out, the Pirate faction also managed to obtain the blueprints. Taking advantage of this, they made minor modifications to the design.

The Apogee P-class ship represents a successful blend of advanced scientific and military technologies, making it ideally suited for pirate-led exploration of space sectors.

This class stands out due to its appearance and the fact that it was assembled piecemeal from the wreckage of destroyed Apogees. Pirates operating Apogees (P) often use them to scout locations - most notably for establishing pirate bases.

The ship can hold its own in one-on-one engagements through the smart use of its powerful shield emitter and strong engines. However, its armor rating makes it seem somewhat fragile on paper, and thus it is rarely deployed in large fleet actions.

Its high construction cost means that only wealthy pirates involved in base building can afford an Apogee P-class fully equipped for aggressive exploration.

A common freighter, refitted by pirates to carry weaponry.

Multiple medium weapon mounts make the Gemini a viable long-range fire support platform. The flight deck is tiny, originally envisioned for mining drone repair or hazardous mining operations. Modern use in the Sector extends its flight deck facilities to all fighter types.

While impressive in a blueprint, the lack of empty, compatible Gemini-type containers in the Sector makes the actual usefulness of the quick-release mechanism negligible. Nonetheless, a decent overall profile, the flight deck, a flexible power core, and good shields make the Gemini a good choice for combat, provided the cost can be weathered.

Formidable pirate vessel! The impressive ship is equipped with top-tier engines, delivering speed and maneuverability that are remarkable for a destroyer. It was quickly repainted in its owner's colors. Numerous energy weapon slots offer a wide range of tactical options.

The Medusa (P) has become one of the few formidable destroyers available to pirates in the Sector - a status stemming from its links to covert operations and elite pirate factions; the numerous attempts by pirates to seize the Medusa (P) serve as a testament to the superiority of its technology.

This widespread use of one class of ship has created the Wayfarer P class.

With respectable armor and armament for a heavy frigate, the Wayfarer (P) does not fit the ruthless economics that would suit it for bulk trade on the dedicated lanes where safety is guaranteed by civilized space. No, the Wayfarer is a starship for lonely runs on the frontier, between worlds where the tough law of necessity reigns, where brigands roam, and the crossed arcs of one's own gun turrets are the best comfort to be found in the cold reach of space.

The Grendel (P) project was fraught with difficulties from the very start; the ship was originally conceived as a heavy phase-capable drone. Losses were considered acceptable and damage routine, for this ship is a true close-quarters brawler - capable of executing a phase-jump through the initial volley of enemy fire to suddenly appear in the heart of the hostile formation, ready to unleash a barrage of missiles and heavy cannon fire. The challenge, of course, lies in safely executing this maneuver, which requires a delicate balance between energy fluctuation levels and positioning - though the Grendel's (P) operational history proves that safe" is hardly the word to describe it.
